preconditions: Identify record, read/propose, apply or reset mode and the actual ledger/configuration path.
Review representative telemetry and independent task evidence before treating aggregate rates as grounds for a shared routing change.
For a configuration write, provide four finite ordered numeric thresholds in the score range and preserve an appropriate prior snapshot when recovery matters.

expected_effects.effect: record appends caller-supplied telemetry; load/analyze aggregate retained lines.
expected_effects.scope: User ~/.botte/control-ledger.jsonl or the explicit path; task excerpt, timestamp, routing fields and returned statistics.
expected_effects.basis: record creates parents and appends UTF-8 JSON best-effort. load skips malformed JSON lines; analyze sums fields and uses success=True when absent.
expected_effects.impact: Can retain private task text and duplicate records on retry. Missing/partial/unrepresentative data or unsupported shapes can bias statistics or prevent analysis.
expected_effects.verification: Inspect the actual ledger, origin of fields, missing failures and repeated execution identities; compare against independent task/usage evidence.

expected_effects.effect: adapt returns a heuristic threshold proposal without writing the configuration.
expected_effects.scope: Explicit aggregate statistics or the shared ledger and current threshold values.
expected_effects.basis: At least ten aggregate samples permit a small LOCAL-boundary step based on success/escalation rates. Explicit thresholds are validated; a step that would break ordering is left unchanged. MCP routing_stats only reads/proposes.
expected_effects.impact: The rationale can appear stronger than the underlying telemetry: aggregate returned-text success is not verified local reliability or a causal comparison.
expected_effects.verification: Capture the input statistics and current configuration; compare candidates on representative target tasks while confirming proposal-only mode made no writes.

expected_effects.effect: apply, adapt --apply and reset atomically replace the routing-threshold configuration after validation.
expected_effects.scope: User ~/.botte/routing-thresholds.json or the explicit destination and subsequent auto_router.effort decisions.
expected_effects.basis: Four finite numeric boundaries must satisfy 0 <= free < local < cheap < standard <= 1 before filesystem mutation. write_json writes a same-directory temporary file, fsyncs and replaces the destination. reset writes defaults.
expected_effects.impact: Changes later model choices across consumers of the shared file. Failed replacement preserves the previous file, but there is no lock or conflict check; reset is not restoration of previous custom values.
expected_effects.verification: Use temporary destinations to test rejected inputs, failed replacement and live-reader/reset behavior; inspect the actual version before and after a real authorized write.

downstream_effects.effect: Later tasks can route differently, changing model quality, latency, data recipients and cost.
downstream_effects.scope: All auto-router consumers sharing the user-level threshold file.
downstream_effects.basis: The effort reader loads thresholds at each decision; malformed configuration falls back to defaults without repairing the file.
downstream_effects.impact: Valid thresholds can still be a poor policy; restoring a file does not reverse decisions already made under earlier values.
downstream_effects.verification: Compare old/new policies against independently evaluated target tasks and measured usage; retain configuration versions and observed decisions.

downstream_effects.effect: Repeated or unverified telemetry can reinforce an unsuitable routing proposal.
downstream_effects.scope: Future aggregates, repeated adaptation steps and downstream policy choices.
downstream_effects.basis: Ledger entries are neither project/model-version scoped nor independently authenticated; missing success defaults true and some router failures/cache hits are absent.
downstream_effects.impact: An apparent improvement can reflect sample selection or repeated events rather than better task completion.
downstream_effects.verification: Use scoped, deduplicated evidence and independent success labels before accepting a candidate or reusing it elsewhere.

reversibility.strategy: Reconcile later writers and restore the intended retained configuration within task scope; reconcile duplicate telemetry and downstream actions separately.
residual_effects: No configuration history archive, cross-resource transaction or automatic rollback is provided.
Consumed inference, disclosed data and decisions already made cannot be undone by resetting thresholds.
An interrupted write can leave a temporary file; ledger append and configuration replacement are separate operations.

retry.check_before_retry: Reads/proposals can be repeated against stable inputs. record appends again; apply/reset replace state and timestamps; a new adapt run can propose a further step. Inspect partial state and concurrent changes first.
retry.stop_condition: Resolve invalid input, unknown writer state, persistence failures or unsupported telemetry before repeating a mutation or treating a proposal as evidence of improvement.

required_scope: Existing task authority for the ledger data, output recipients and a shared routing-policy change when applying/resetting. Read-only statistics and returned proposals grant no authority for deployment, training or model activation.

analysis.summary: The module records telemetry and offers heuristic changes with explicit application. Input and replacement checks protect configuration structure, not the empirical quality of a policy or its underlying labels.
uncertainties: AutoRouter telemetry is best-effort and does not include every attempt; returned-text success and local token totals are not independent quality/savings measurements.
Ledgers are shared by user account and have no automatic retention, provenance verification, deduplication or complete record-shape validation.
auto_router.effort validation/defaults, atomic_json writing, executing consumers and runtime state are outside these skill-local source bindings.
Atomic replacement has no compare-and-swap, snapshot archive or full observation adapter; successful persistence does not prove which later decisions read it.
Atomic replacement uses temporary-file permissions and replaces a destination symlink; existing file metadata and cross-account access are not preserved automatically.

reuse.target: Evaluate a threshold proposal offline for another task-scoped routing policy.
reuse.rationale: Explicit records, statistics, thresholds and paths allow a controlled candidate/current comparison before shared configuration changes.
adaptations: Bind evidence to task/model/configuration versions and independent success labels; include failures and deduplicate executions.
Use isolated destinations, preserve rollback state and measure actual quality, usage and recipients.
reuse.validation: Replay representative tasks for current and candidate thresholds, record independently assessed outcomes and measured costs, and verify persistence/failure/recovery behavior in the target context.
